Northrop Grumman Mission Systems Long Range Air Defense & Domestic Systems (LRAD & DS) Operating Unit specializes in the development, manufacture, assembly, testing, and sustainment of international Air Surveillance Sensors and Systems, Bio-detection systems, and Air Traffic Control capabilities. This is a worldwide international business with customers in North Africa, Middle East, Southeast Asia and South and Central America.  We are seeking a Program Management Senior Director to join our team of qualified and diverse individuals. This position will be located in Elkridge, MD.

The position has P&L responsibility for management, strategy, and execution including establishing a strong trajectory for growing the business. This position reports to the VP, Land & Maritime Sensors Business Unit. In addition, this position has significant senior leadership contact and will require a candidate with strong leadership and decision-making skills with the ability to perform in an environment of ambiguity and continuous change. The position must role model leadership values and behaviors. The candidate must have strong communication, executive presence, and cross-cultural skills to be able to effectively interact with a geographically disbursed senior leadership team.

- Lead the negotiation of contracts, contract changes, specifications, operating budgets, schedule milestones, and key terms and conditions.
- Proactively identify trends, risks, and opportunities within the organization and develop solutions in partnership with peers, division and matrix leadership, and regional/division HR business leaders

- Analyze and concisely present information to the management team to enable good business decisions

- Bachelor’s degree with 15 or more years of program management or related experience; OR Master's degree with 12 or more years of program management or related experience. Minimum 7 years of international program management with DCS contracts in at least two diverse geographical regions.

- Experience with US Export Regulations /licensing processes and their applicability to Foreign DCS and FMS contracts
- Expertise in program execution to lead the performance of tasks on schedule and at cost on Development and Production programs
- International Capture and Proposal management experience
- Proven success in leading and influencing individuals and teams in a matrix environment
- Demonstrated ability to foster existing customer relationships and develop new customer relationships
- Strong communication and executive presence skills to effectively interact with customer and senior leadership

Northrop Grumman Mission Systems (NGMS) is looking for you to join our team as a  Principal Operations Program Management Specialist (Principal Production Operations) based in  Rolling Meadows, IL.   This role is full-time onsite.

The candidate will support production, development, business, and other processes in a team-based manufacturing environment. - Bachelor’s degree and a minimum of 5 years of related work experience; OR a Master’s degree and 3 or more years of relevant work experience; OR 9 years relevant work experience in lieu of a degree.

- Experience with Material Requirements Planning (MRP).

- Experience with Microsoft Office (Excel, PowerPoint, and Word).

- Ability to obtain and maintain a US Government Secret Clearance.

- US Citizenship required.

- Experience with taking a prototype to full rate production

- Experience in the defense/aerospace industry

- Experience performing in a fast-paced manufacturing and development environment.

- In-depth experience with Manufacturing Resource Planning (MRP), production planning, and material management

jobs.title: Supply Operations Lead
jobs.description:
AUSTRALIAN CITIZENSHIP REQUIRED FOR THIS POSITION: Yes

RELOCATION ASSISTANCE: Relocation assistance may be available

CLEARANCE TYPE: AU- Secret (NV1)

TRAVEL: No

Description

At Northrop Grumman Australia, our work contributes to some of the nation's most important Defence capabilities. As part of the MQ-4C Triton program, you'll play a critical role in ensuring aircraft, tooling and equipment are available when and where they're needed to support operational success. This is an opportunity to lead a high-performing logistics team, influence continuous improvement initiatives, and make a tangible impact within a complex Defence environment.

Your role:
As Supply Operations Lead, you'll lead a team responsible for warehouse, inventory, distribution and tooling operations supporting the Triton program. You'll ensure critical assets are received, stored, maintained and delivered safely, efficiently and in compliance with Defence and regulatory requirements.

Working closely with Defence stakeholders, maintenance teams and suppliers, you'll drive operational excellence, develop your team, manage inventory performance, coordinate freight activities, and identify opportunities to improve logistics processes across the program.

Key responsibilities include:
- Leading and developing a team of warehousing professionals, including workforce planning, training, performance management and quality oversight.
- Managing inventory, stock accuracy, warehousing operations and distribution activities to support Triton maintenance and operational requirements.
- Overseeing receipt, storage, inspection, picking, packing and dispatch of aircraft and non-aircraft parts.
- Coordinating inbound and outbound freight movements and supporting complex logistics activities across multiple stakeholders.
- Managing tooling, ground support equipment (GSE) and calibration activities to ensure operational readiness.
- Maintaining compliance with Defence, export control, warehousing and safety requirements, including ITAR obligations.
- Driving governance, reporting and continuous improvement initiatives across warehousing and distribution functions.
- Building strong relationships with Defence personnel, suppliers, freight partners and internal program teams to achieve operational outcomes.

About you:
You're a people-focused logistics professional who enjoys leading teams, solving complex operational challenges and delivering exceptional customer outcomes. You thrive in a fast-paced, highly regulated environment and bring a strong understanding of warehousing, inventory management and supply chain operations.

You'll bring:
- Experience leading warehousing, logistics or supply chain operations, ideally within Defence, aviation or a similarly regulated industry.
- Strong leadership skills with the ability to motivate and develop high-performing teams.
- Experience managing inventory, distribution and warehouse compliance activities.
- The ability to build trusted relationships with Defence, suppliers and internal stakeholders.
- Knowledge of Defence logistics systems such as MILIS and CAMM2.
- Strong communication, problem-solving and continuous improvement skills.
- Ability to obtain and maintain an ADF NV1 Security Clearance.
- Dangerous Cargo Handling Certification (desirable).
- Current Forklift Licence (desirable).

Join a team where your expertise helps sustain a critical Defence capability, your ideas are valued, and your professional growth is supported. At Northrop Grumman Australia, you'll be empowered to solve complex challenges, collaborate with talented professionals and contribute to work that protects Australia's future.

What we offer:
Whatever your role, life stage or background, you can shape your career here in your way with highly challenging work, great colleagues and career development, plus a range of flexible benefits and working patterns.
- Professional development – further education, leadership development, professional industry memberships and unlimited access to a range of online training
- Salary packaging including novated car leases and the option to purchase additional annual leave
- Flexible working options, including hybrid working, 9 day fortnights, volunteer leave and varying start and finish times to suit your family needs
- 18 weeks paid parental leave and 2 weeks paid reservist leave
- We offer all employees access to our Health & Wellbeing program and Employee Assistance program
- Employee Discount Program
- Employee Recognition Program

For more information or a confidential discussion, please contact hayley.bincalar@au.ngc.com

As a Defence security clearance is required for this role, you must be an Australian Citizen. International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) are applicable, as such your nationality may be a factor in determining your suitability for this role. You will also need to satisfy police checks and employment screening verification
